description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:88-124 introduces a new public type IoFailure to satisfy AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (cache-friendly result types must be Clone+Eq+Send+Sync, optionally Serialize). This is currently the only such type in the workspace.

Sibling adapter crates that will eventually need an io-error equivalent in their cache-friendly error types:
  - pkix-truststore-system (per PKIX-8h87) — will do file I/O for /etc/ssl/certs/* on Linux/BSD, plus FFI calls that produce errors.
  - pkix-truststore-pkcs11 (per PKIX-p8vz) — PKCS#11 errors are not io::Error but it will likely do file I/O for module discovery.
  - pkix-revocation-http — already exists; does HTTP fetch and will need io-error and net-error boundary types.
  - any future cloud-KMS adapter.

Three paths forward:
  a) Each adapter reinvents IoFailure (or an analog). This duplicates the wire-form contract and the Debug-of-ErrorKind brittleness across N crates.
  b) Each adapter depends on pkix-truststore solely to re-use IoFailure. That makes pkix-truststore a transitive dep of pkix-revocation-http etc., which is not architecturally clean (pkix-truststore is a Tier-1 trust-anchor loader, not an io-utility crate).
  c) Lift IoFailure into pkix-path or a small pkix-shared crate, and have pkix-truststore re-export it (similar to the DerError pattern).

Option (c) is the right shape and matches how DerError already lives in pkix-path and is re-exported. Pre-1.0 this move is cheap; post-1.0 it is a semver event.

If the answer is "we will not have other adapters needing this" — that conflicts with PKIX-8h87 and PKIX-p8vz which both involve file I/O for adapter discovery.
title: IoFailure invented in pkix-truststore; will need to be replicated or re-exported by sibling adapter crates
